title: Tenali Raman Tale 74

full_text:
A wealthy, arrogant nobleman named Gundappa was notorious in Vijayanagara for insulting his hosts. Whenever he was invited to a wedding or family feast, he would taste the delicacies, grimace in disgust, and loudly criticize the cooking:
'The rice is too soft! The sambar lacks asafoetida! The payasam is too watery! No one in this city understands culinary refinement like I do!'
Hosts trembled in dread whenever Gundappa visited.

Tenali Raman decided to cure the pompous critic once and for all.
Tenali sent an ornate invitation to Gundappa:
'Noble Lord Gundappa, I have hired the legendary master chefs of the Chola empire to prepare an exclusive Twelve-Course Imperial Feast in your honor at my home.'

Flattered beyond measure, Gundappa arrived in his finest silks, boasting of his refined palate.
Tenali seated him upon a velvet cushion and served the feast upon a fresh banana leaf.

First course: A steaming, fragrant green vegetable soup.
Gundappa took a large spoonful—and his face immediately contorted in horrific agony!
The soup was intensely, excruciatingly bitter!
Tenali smiled politely: 'That is our Imperial Starter: Crushed Wild Bitter Gourd Soup!'

Second course: Crispy fried fritters.
Gundappa took a bite, hoping for relief—it was sliced raw bitter gourd coated in bitter neem paste!
Third course: A dark curry—pure bitter gourd stewed in bitter fenugreek water!
Fourth course: Rice mixed with bitter gourd juice!
Even the sweet pudding at the end was bitter gourd boiled in bitter melon pulp!

Gundappa dropped his silver spoon, tears streaming from his eyes, his mouth burning with intense bitterness:
'Tenali! Art thou trying to poison me? Every single dish is made of bitter gourd! There is not a grain of salt, sugar, or sweetness in this entire feast!'

Tenali Raman looked at him with innocent, wide eyes:
'Why, noble Lord Gundappa! You have spent twenty years spitting out the sweet feasts of honest families, complaining that everything is sour, watery, or flawed!
I thought that a gentleman whose tongue is filled with so much constant bitterness could only appreciate food that matches the flavor of his own speech!
I had my cooks prepare an entire banquet of bitterness to honor your natural disposition!'

Gundappa sat in stunned silence. The biting truth of Tenali’s culinary satire struck him to the core.
He realized how deeply his rude, ungrateful complaints had hurt innocent hosts for decades.
Gundappa bowed his head in genuine shame:
'Tenali, forgive me. My tongue was indeed bitter, and thou hast served me the mirror of my own words.'

Tenali smiled warmly, ordered the bitter gourd cleared away, and brought out a magnificent, delicious feast of sweet coconut rice, mango pachadi, and creamy payasam.
Gundappa ate with humble gratitude, and never again spoke an insulting word at another man’s table.
moral: Pretentious gourmets who complain endlessly about simple hospitality deserve a taste of unvarnished bitterness.
